page: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-12 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the g4 server family. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture and is equipped with 45.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 3.75 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include any local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes.

A key feature of the g4-standard-12 instance is its fractional GPU allocation. It is provisioned with 0.25 of an NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 GPU, which is built on the Ada Lovelace architecture. This configuration provides access to a portion of the GPU's resources, including its 24 GB of total VRAM, making it suitable for workloads that require hardware acceleration but do not demand a full, dedicated GPU.

By offering a fractional GPU slice alongside 12 dedicated vCPUs, this instance provides a cost-efficient entry point for graphics-heavy and GPU-accelerated tasks without the expense of a whole GPU. It is designed for workloads such as entry-level 3D rendering, remote workstations, model inference, and general-purpose tasks that benefit from moderate GPU acceleration.
